lessonRef.title: Correction and reflection: wiping up and putting away

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Ready for Life elementary sequence — Grade 3
Ready for Life v1 safety, supervision, and no-shame policy reference
Manuel Academy RFL G3 Unit 3 — kitchen helper safety and no-heat preparation
objective: Learners review and practice the end-of-task cleanup routine (rinsing and stacking non-sharp dishes like a cup or bowl near the sink, wiping the cleared counter or table with a damp cloth, returning small tools such as spoons to their storage drawer, and doing a final look-over) by naming what got left undone after a past kitchen task and correcting it on their own counter or table.
scenario: Thinking back to the last time they or someone else helped in the kitchen, the learner walks through a four-step wiping-and-putting-away routine on a real counter or table that has a cup, bowl, or spoon left on it: moving the dishes near the sink first, wiping the cleared surface with a damp cloth, returning small tools to their exact drawer or shelf, and doing one final look-over before calling the space done.
safetyNotes: Always ask a trusted adult before rinsing or touching any dish that might have been used with raw food.
Stick to non-sharp items like cups, bowls, and spoons; leave any knife for an adult to handle.
materials: a counter or table with a cup, bowl, or spoon left on it
a drawer or shelf where small tools belong

tasks.directions: Think back to the last time you or someone else helped in the kitchen.

prompts.text: Name one specific thing that got left out or not put away after that task.

tasks.directions: Run the four-step wiping-and-putting-away routine in order: move dishes near the sink, wipe the cleared surface with a damp cloth, return small tools to their exact spot, and finish with a final look-over.

prompts.text: I rinsed and stacked any cup, bowl, or spoon near the sink instead of leaving it on the counter.
I wiped the counter or table surface with a damp cloth until crumbs and spills were gone.
I returned small tools, like a spoon or a measuring cup, to the exact drawer or shelf they belong in.
I did one final look-over of the whole space before calling it done.

tasks.directions: Without this checklist in front of you, run the same four steps again tomorrow after a different snack or meal, from memory.

prompts.text: List the four wiping-and-putting-away steps from memory. Which one is easiest to forget?

tasks.directions: Compare today's cleanup to the thing you noticed was left undone in task one.

prompts.text: Explain specifically how today's four-step cleanup would have prevented the thing you noticed was left undone earlier.

remediation: If a learner wipes the counter but leaves dishes sitting on it instead of moving them near the sink first, reteach by having them do the steps in a fixed order, dishes off the counter first and then wipe, so the surface being wiped is always fully clear before the cloth touches it.
extension: Have the learner apply the same four-step wiping-and-putting-away routine to a different shared space, like a bathroom counter after brushing teeth or a craft table after a project, naming what changes and what stays the same about the routine.
